episodes.179399: Scattered thunderstorms, a few strong, developed during the afternoon and lasted into the early evening hours. One of the thunderstorms produced nickel sized hail in Franklin County.
episodes.179516: A shortwave that turned into a baggy trough over eastern Texas provided Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley with several rounds of showers and storms June 3rd through June 5th. Large hail fell in a storm just northwest of Rio Grande City on June 3rd before turning into a sub-severe line of showers and storms across the populated Rio Grande Valley. ||Northwesterly flow aloft on the southwestern side of the trough led to several more showers and storms across the eastern half of Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley on June 4th. The storms headed south from Corpus Christi's area and moved along the coast of Kenedy and Willacy Counties before moving southwestward into Cameron County where it produced very large hail, up to 2.5 in diameter, and 80 mph wind gusts at Valley International Airport in Harlingen. Additional storms flared up in Hidalgo County and produced 1 hail. ||The storms on June 5th followed a similar script to June 4th with storms along the coast of Kenedy and Willacy Counties before developing inland. While the storms weren't as strong, they still produced large hail in northern Cameron County and 50 to 60 mph wind gusts near Brownsville.
episodes.179546: An upper-level low off the coast of California helped funnel in subtropical moisture into the state resulting in the development of widespread showers and storms across central and eastern New Mexico June 5th and 6th. Reports of severe weather and flash flooding stretched from the Rio Grande Valley across portions of eastern NM on June 5th. These reports ranged from a landspout tornado near the Petroglyph National Monument and Nara Visa, NM to flash flooding. Another round of severe weather began in the afternoon of June 6th producing more widespread reports over the same area of the state. Reports ranged from burn scar flash flooding within the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar and Santa Rosa, to large hail over parts of San Miguel County.
episodes.179690: An upper-level low swirling over eastern Texas allowed for the formation of supercell thunderstorms along the coast both June 4th and June 5th. Rincon del San Jose was hit both days with gusts over 40 knots June 4th and near 60 knots on June 5th.
episodes.179731: Storms developed during the afternoon and early evening along and south of a stationary front extending from northwest to southeast Missouri. Sporadic wind damage and small hail to the size of pennies occurred with the stronger storm.
episodes.179781: Heavy rain fell from thunderstorms and produced a couple of debris flows Sunday evening.
episodes.180267: Showers and thunderstorms produced gusty outflow winds and a brief tornado.
episodes.180667: A surface low pressure center moved into the far southwestern portion of the state. At the upper levels ridging was positioned across the Southwestern United States and the opportunity presented itself for thunderstorm development ahead of the trough that was placed across the Central Plains. The severe storms that developed posed a severe wind and hail threat across the central and northern parts of Arkansas.
episodes.180860: Midlevel system provided sufficient lift for isolated severe thunderstorms to produce large hail across eastern Tennessee.
episodes.180861: Weak frontal boundary moved across the state, generating scattered severe thunderstorms that produced hail and damaging winds.
episodes.181230: A lingering upper-level trough stretching from the Texas Panhandle southeastward into Louisiana and along the northern Gulf coast provided the necessary forcing for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop across parts of North Louisiana late on June 4th. By the mid to late afternoon hours, thunderstorms began to develop in a modestly unstable air mass with the greatest coverage extending from Deep East Texas into portions of North Louisiana. A few thunderstorms reached severe limits with multiple local storm reports of large hail and damaging wind gusts scattered across North Louisiana throughout the late afternoon hours.
episodes.181317: Several ordinary-type thunderstorms developed from the early afternoon into evening of the 5th across the forecast area. One of these storms produced severe hail and a damaging downburst wind event in the southern Oklahoma City metropolitan area.
episodes.181715: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the late afternoon and evening of the 5th. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to half dollar size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.181790: Small scattered storms developed during the afternoon of June 5th and produced a few large hail and strong wind reports.
episodes.182020: Diurnally driven thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and early evening of June 5th, 2023 across south central Kansas.  The pulse severe thunderstorms were slow moving and produced sporadic reports of quarter sized hail and wind gusts of 58 to 67 mph.
episodes.182332: A weak, ill-defined, cold front pushed into the Mid-South during the afternoon hours on June 5, 2023. The front interacted with a marginally unstable airmass to produce scattered thunderstorms. A few storms became severe with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.182333: A weak, ill-defined, cold front pushed into the Mid-South during the afternoon hours on June 5, 2023. The front interacted with a marginally unstable airmass to produce scattered thunderstorms. A few storms became severe with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.182334: A weak, ill-defined, cold front pushed into the Mid-South during the afternoon hours on June 5, 2023. The front interacted with a marginally unstable airmass to produce scattered thunderstorms. A few storms became severe with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.182363: An isolated strong storm over the gulf coastal waters produce a strong wind gust.
episodes.182393: A fairly typical summertime regime was in place with abundant Gulf moisture throughout the atmosphere. As the day progressed, sea breeze boundaries became the focal point for thunderstorm initiation and ample instability enhanced intensity of a few storms that resulted in severe marine wind gusts.
episodes.182394: A fairly typical summertime regime was in place with abundant Gulf moisture throughout the atmosphere. As the day progressed, sea breeze boundaries became the focal point for thunderstorm initiation and ample instability enhanced intensity of a few storms that resulted in severe wind gusts and hail.
episodes.182792: Storms on the afternoon and evening of June 5th brought hail and strong winds to eastern Kansas.
episodes.182852: A thunderstorm produced wind gusts near 45 knots near Baffin Bay.
episodes.183027: Thunderstorms in the Devils Lake Basin produced high wind gusts around 60 - 65 MPH.
episodes.183099: Scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi on June 5th and 6th. A few of the storms became severe and produced damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.183323: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening across northeast Georgia. One of the storms produced large hail across Habersham County.
episodes.184608: The combination of afternoon instability as well as increasing mid-level moisture pushing northward on the eastern flank of an upper level low that moved over SoCal and stalled over central-southern California. This upper feature introduced a daily chance of showers and thunderstorms during the first week of June.
